_about: gump measured results and corrections, read from the repo 2026-11-14. status: proved | measured-and-rechecked (CLAIMS level A/B) | measured (level C/none) | forecast | unchecked | retired. ln_tau = natural log of generations; se = 1 s.e. as quoted. Newest correction wins. Path abbreviations in src: REV=research/audit/REVIEW-gpu-pr8.md; AUD=research/AUDIT-2026-11-13.md; FP=research/fluct/PREDICTIONS.md; GP=research/gpu/PREDICTIONS.md; XP=research/theory/exponent/PREDICTIONS.md; TP=research/toy2d/PREDICTIONS.md; FR=research/fluct/README.md; GR=research/gpu/README.md; LR=research/lineage/README.md; TR=research/toy2d/README.md; NB 11-XX=research/NOTEBOOK.md (dated entry 2026-11-XX); CL=research/CLAIMS.md (row); ST=research/STATUS.md; SYMCSV=research/fluct/data/sym_residence.csv; QSD=research/fluct/data/qsd_summary.json; SYMFIT=research/fluct/sym_fit.py; GPUDATA/=research/data/gpu_facelaw/; BOARD=research/theory/swarm/critic/board.md; PEEL/=research/peeling/; EXP/=research/experiments/

octahedral_engine.label: Octahedral faces, CPU ensembles
octahedral_engine.line: Each extra cell in a face makes it live about e^0.21 times longer.
octahedral_engine.note: asymmetric p=0.35 soups in hull |p|_1<=R; tau_face = 8 x first-peel mean after T0=200

octahedral_gpu.label: Bigger faces on rented GPUs
octahedral_gpu.line: Faces of 108 and 135 cells, run on graphics cards, cost more per cell than smaller ones.
octahedral_gpu.src: GR "First use"; GPUDATA R*_A10G.json; NB 11-13 GPU
octahedral_gpu.note: reviewer re-derived tables, emulated kernel on CPU; lead re-derived 108/135 from raw deaths; no 2nd implementation at A>=108; A=135 ages <= 1/900 of mean

local_slopes.label: Cost per cell keeps rising
local_slopes.line: From small to large faces the price of each extra cell climbs from 0.201 to 0.221.
local_slopes.src: FR lead note; GR; REV claim 2 item 6
local_slopes.curvature: A=108 is 0.21+-0.04 nats above the line through verified A=45-84; curvature 2.6 sigma (GPU only), ~5 sigma with CPU; limit unknown

slab_faces.label: Flat faces without rims
slab_faces.line: Flat faces with no edges follow one straight line: each cell adds 0.209 to the log lifetime.
slab_faces.src: PEEL/slab_area.csv, m=8 rows chosen by PEEL/face_law_fit.py
slab_faces.note: computed by me: ln_tau = ln(2 x mean_first), se = (ln ci_hi - ln ci_lo)/3.92; 512 replicas each

periodic_slab_2nd_agent.label: Rim-free faces, second agent
periodic_slab_2nd_agent.line: Another agent found rim-free faces also get slightly costlier per cell as they grow.
periodic_slab_2nd_agent.note: 12-layer periodic slab; exponent study not written up or checked (ST)

retired_fits.label: Gaussian guess at zero
retired_fits.line: A bell-curve guess at the empty-face odds overshot, giving 0.28-0.30 per cell.
retired_fits.why: tail straight to n=1; extrapolating from x>=0.1 misses ln h by 0.5-0.8 nats

retired_fits.label: Lead's slope 0.199
retired_fits.line: The lead's first check came from an unlucky sample; the slope there is 0.212.
retired_fits.src: NB 11-12 check + note I1; CL F7
retired_fits.why: 1.7 sigma high draw of 240 runs; 2300 gives 0.212

retired_fits.label: The 0.2077 endpoint fit
retired_fits.line: A four-point curve claimed 0.2077 per cell; it missed its own data by 28 error bars.
retired_fits.src: FR lead note (late); BOARD E2; CL GP4
retired_fits.why: misses A=45 by 0.08 nats (28 se); slopes rise
retired_fits.by: swarm critic E2; retired by lead

retired_fits.label: GPU "13 sigma" bend
retired_fits.line: The GPU first measured its big face against the bad line; the real excess is 0.21 nats.

retired_fits.label: Octahedral 1.2-1.8x tougher
retired_fits.line: Octahedral faces are 1.7-1.9 times tougher than flat ones, not 1.2-1.8.
retired_fits.src: NB 11-12 peeling note W3; CL F6
retired_fits.why: counted runs whose hull shrank before t0; now 2,287, CV 1.03

retired_fits.label: Ten to the 41, measured?
retired_fits.line: The 10^41-generation figure is a fivefold extrapolation, never a measurement.
retired_fits.said: side-13 hull, asymmetric: ~1e41 gens per face, tagged measured
retired_fits.why: law measured A<=90, used at 459; now conjecture

firewall.label: Cutting through costs less per cell
firewall.line: An interior cut costs 0.12 per cell but needs more cells; it wins only in thin slabs.
firewall.fit: ln tau_fw = -1.4 + 0.54 N m + 0.22 N (14 batches, N=4-7, rms 0.27)
firewall.who_wins: switches firewall->peel at m~N; N=4 firewall first 397/512 (m=4), 175 (5), 35 (6); N=5: 426 (5), 93 (6); octahedra: always peeling

cpu.label: Symmetric faces, CPU
cpu.line: Symmetric faces die far sooner than lopsided ones of equal size, yet still exponentially in size.
cpu.note: O_h soups p=0.35, T0=1000, tau=exposure/deaths; c cube-, v vertex-centred; pooled 693: v soups 45 deaths 7.1e8, c 58 deaths 3.5e8 (NB 11-13)

gpu.label: Symmetric faces on GPUs
gpu.line: Graphics cards pushed symmetric faces to 828 cells; all three forecasts written beforehand held.
gpu.caveat: cube-centred hazard falls with age (Weibull 0.94, 0.84; p 0.04, 0.01)

fits.label: Effective area A/7.7
fits.line: Treating a symmetric face as a fixed fraction of a normal one worked only to about 460 cells.
fits.why: low by x1.9 at 570, x2.3 at 630; side 16 outlived it

fits.label: First curved fit
fits.line: An early curved fit on less data was replaced by a refit.

fits.label: Six locked copies, minus edges
fits.line: A symmetric face acts like six locked copies of one patch, less a penalty along mirror lines.
fits.present: current; 0.14/0.25 nats below GPU 759/828; slope imposed (BOARD E5)

fits.label: Free fits disagree far out
fits.line: Equally good curves differ by half a nat at 828 cells; the true slope is not pinned down.

vertex_cube_factor.label: Vertex-centred faces last longer
vertex_cube_factor.line: Faces centred on a lattice corner outlast cube-centred ones of equal size by about one and a half.
vertex_cube_factor.retired: 3.3 (FR correction 3) and 3.1 (NB 11-13): leaned on cube copies

legacy_cubes.label: The closed cubes, sides 8-16
legacy_cubes.line: Each bigger cube lived far longer; side 16 lasted almost three billion generations.
legacy_cubes.src: docs/AUTOMATON.md sec 4; NB 11-12 legacy ash, engine, cubes 14/15; NB 11-13 side 16; PEEL/cube_lifetime.csv
legacy_cubes.claims: R1-R4, F1, F3, C1 B, C2 B
legacy_cubes.convention: lifetime = cycle_start; 14 and 16 quoted as detected_gen (cycle_start 4,460,296 and 2,919,617,675)

tail_table.label: Odds of a nearly empty face
tail_table.line: Each cell fewer on a face is about two-thirds as likely, straight down to the last cell.
tail_table.note: ln P(n=k) per face-generation, k=1..39; 137,243 deaths

death_rate_vs_p1.label: Death is the next step down
death_rate_vs_p1.line: The death rate sits where the straight line lands one step past one cell.

single_cell_share.label: Most faces die from one cell
single_cell_share.line: Nearly two in three faces die from a single surviving cell, at every size.

final_plunge.label: Ordinary until the very end
final_plunge.line: A dying face looks normal until about sixteen generations before death, then falls in ten to twelve.
final_plunge.splitting: clone fates 55-95% correlated; FFS gains nothing

three_cell_remnant.label: The last ember: a triangle
three_cell_remnant.line: The usual three-cell remnant is a small triangle of faces round one cube corner.
three_cell_remnant.detail: 38% of 3-cell faces; lasts 1.9 gens mean (max 15); then grows 60%, dies 1%; 2-cell faces an edge pair 54%

headline.label: Cube-like seeds wait like soups
headline.line: Over a thousand runs from cube-like starts waited like random ones, with no memory between steps.
headline.rerun: lineage_check.py re-run by me: matches NB

cube_plateaus.label: Sixteen cube plateaus versus average
cube_plateaus.line: Side 16 sat on one step 7.4 times the average wait; most other steps look ordinary.

slow_variable.label: States remember a little
slow_variable.line: Copies of a state live slightly longer when the original did; real but weak.

double_peels.label: Sometimes two layers go together
double_peels.line: Rarely the next layer dies right after the first, within a few generations.
double_peels.src: LR sec 3; GR "Second use"; REV claim 4

tau_R40.label: Two averages at radius 40
tau_R40.line: Mixing copies of the cube into the average made it look shorter than fresh random starts give.
tau_R40.reason: pool includes side-16 cube copies (2.875e9 copies alone 5.73e7)

toy2d.label: A two-dimensional cousin
toy2d.line: A flat version of the rule does the same: edges die after waits exponential in their length.
toy2d.rule: B34/S234, square lattice, cross (+-1,0),(+-2,0),(0,+-1),(0,+-2): alive iff n+x>=3, but n>=5 dies
toy2d.vessel: strips 16 x L, periodic along edge
corrected: line rejected; ln L term 0.374+-0.009; L>=20 0.410+-0.003 (BOARD E1)
strip tau saturated: transverse 3-column cuts now events (TR 4.4)
lead's first check counted settled debris (tau ~20,000 at L=12)

forecasts.label: Side 16, before the run
forecasts.line: Before side 16 ran it was forecast at 240 million generations; it lived twelve times longer.

forecasts.label: Side 16, curved fits
forecasts.line: Revised fits made at one billion still put the first face loss too early.

forecasts.label: First face, from copies
forecasts.line: Sixty-four nudged copies of the running cube forecast the first face loss; it fell inside.

forecasts.label: Second face, from fits
forecasts.line: The fit-only forecast of the second face loss just caught it, at its edge.

forecasts.label: Second face, from copies
forecasts.line: Copies said the second face would go much sooner; the cube held on far longer.

forecasts.label: Side 17 first plateau
forecasts.line: Side 17 was forecast at 26 billion generations per face; symmetric soups on GPUs gave 32 billion.

forecasts.label: GPU symmetric, 759 and 828
forecasts.line: The GPU agent wrote three symmetric-face forecasts before running; all three held.

forecasts.label: GPU lineages memoryless
forecasts.line: Single random-start runs were forecast to forget their past; they did.
forecasts.result: hit; R=40 tau miss vs pooled 7.1e7 only

forecasts.label: Lead expectation, big faces
forecasts.line: The lead expected big lopsided faces to die sooner than they did.

forecasts.label: 2D symmetry forecasts
forecasts.line: Of six 2D symmetry forecasts, four hit, one half-missed and one missed.
items: F5a diag mirror tau x2 -> 1.0-1.16 half
F5b C4 slope kept -> 0.274 vs 0.343 miss

forecasts.line: A theory agent scored its own forecasts openly: several hits, several misses, some still open.
items: F1 hit (a miss, b half, c hit, d miss)

rows: Six face-law corrections are listed with the retired fits.
The lead quoted the wrong density of the chaos twice; other agents found 0.4155.
docs/WHAT-I-SEE.md "Where I was wrong"; AUD W2
Faces and interior cuts cost different amounts per cell; there is no single price.
cheapest cut, one cost per cell
The automaton itself refuted the forecast by living twelve times longer.
The corner-centred advantage stays near 1.5; the larger value leaned on cube copies.
A correction blamed start time; the real cause was an unlucky sample.
The odds of an emptying face fall in a straight line, not a flattening curve.
The odds counted the very plateaus that raised suspicion; without them nothing stands out.
The comparison average had cube copies mixed in; with fresh soups the oddity weakens.
The side-19 lifetime is a guess far beyond the data, now with one range.
Two side-17 numbers looked different because one was a mean and one a median.
A handful of small numerical slips were fixed; none changed a conclusion.
e^-5.3; A/8.0 vs A/7.7; 1.5e9; mixed lifetime convention
One sampler counted frozen debris as living faces at small sizes; the engine is used there.
qsd.py sym fine at all R
A reviewer kept every GPU number but corrected four ways they were described.
qsd.py flaw at R=36; tau(40v) +21%; aftershock 0.01 tau
no number biased; pooled vs soup; double peels
Identical death times across machines showed three runs had repeated the same starts.
The 2D slope is not a clean 0.416; the honest range is about 0.36 to 0.41.
Long 2D strips died by a cut across, not at an edge; cuts now count separately.
Rotation symmetry shortened 2D lifetimes, against the forecast; not understood.
The swarm critic's list of corrections lives on its own board.
covered by another agent; E10: Lemma A(c) in exponent/theorems.md false
